gen_risks.description: Geopolitical volatility in the MENA region could disrupt private capital markets, deter regional VC investors, and reduce startup investment flow into Jordan.
gen_risks.mitigation: Position ISSF as a strategic co-investment partner providing non-subsidized matching capital and side letters to de-risk investment terms for international funds.
gen_risks.evidence: Jordan’s small, open economy continues to face vulnerabilities tied to its position in a geopolitically volatile region.

gen_risks.description: High global and local interest rates and VC market downturns may prevent beneficiary startups and funds from mobilizing the targeted $150 million in private capital.
gen_risks.mitigation: Target diverse early-stage fund models, leverage DFI partnerships such as IFC, and mandate 1x minimum investment multiples in fund side letters.
gen_risks.evidence: macro challenges (e.g., Covid-19 pandemic, increased interest rates locally and globally, geopolitical tensions in the region)

gen_risks.description: High turnover of key technical and management personnel in the ISSF PMU could delay capital deployment, M&E reporting, and due diligence execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain competitive market-based compensation structures and institutionalize operational procedures within the Project Operations Manual to retain PMU staff capacity.
gen_risks.evidence: In the initial years of operation, ISSF faced challenges linked to, for example, high turnover of the team.

gen_risks.description: Excessive concentration of capital in a single VC fund or large investment could lead to significant financial loss if that intermediary fails.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce strict investment caps per fund (e.g., US$5 million cap and maximum 30% ownership) as updated in the POM and Investment Strategy.
gen_risks.evidence: To mitigate and manage concentration risks, the current ISSF Investment Strategy sets out the limit on ISSF investment in one VC fund.

gen_risks.description: Supported ICT startups may improperly manage e-waste and hardware disposal, causing environmental pollution and health and safety risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate mandatory environmental screening and good e-waste management/recycling clauses into sub-project legal agreements and the ESMS.
gen_risks.evidence: SMEs’ supported activities may cause environmental impacts connected to mismanagement of e-waste, including pollution, Occupational Health and Safety

gen_risks.description: ISSF PMU's lack of prior direct experience with the World Bank's ESF standards could result in weak environmental and social risk monitoring across financial intermediaries.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire a dedicated Environmental and Social officer and require all partner VC funds to adopt ESMS systems satisfactory to World Bank standards.
gen_risks.evidence: hence, ISSF requires improved E&S risks and impacts management capacity, especially in the implementation of the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards

gen_risks.description: ICT startups funded by the project may lack non-discrimination, workplace safety, and anti-sexual harassment policies, violating social standards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate explicit non-discrimination, worker grievance, and SEA/SH prevention requirements into the Project Operations Manual and fund covenants.
gen_risks.evidence: Additional labor risks related to ICT start-ups include terms and conditions of employment, discrimination, and sexual harassment

gen_risks.description: The current legal corporate duration of ISSF as a Private Shareholding Company ends in 2029, prior to the expected 10-12 year venture investment return lifecycle.
gen_risks.mitigation: Amend ISSF's Articles of Association prior to effectiveness to convert it into an open-ended Private Shareholding Company.
gen_risks.evidence: whereas currently the ISSF Private Shareholding Company ‘ends’ in 2029.

gen_risks.description: The existing Grievance Mechanism at ISSF may not be fully accessible to all project-affected stakeholders or sub-project workers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Upgrade the GM system with safe, confidential, survivor-centered uptake channels and clear resolution procedures across all portfolio levels.
gen_risks.evidence: it was found that the GM system requires enhancement to ensure that all affected parties and stakeholders of the project can access it

gen_risks.description: Delays in authorizing the Subsidiary Agreement between MOPIC and ISSF or adopting the POM could delay loan effectiveness and capital disbursement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Complete the authorization of the Subsidiary Agreement and draft POM/Corporate Governance Manual updates as legal conditions precedent to effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: The Subsidiary Agreement has been duly authorized by the Borrower and ISSF and is legally binding

gen_risks.description: Direct equity co-investments in startups under Component 2 expose ISSF to total single-venture failure risk and cumulative exposure across components.
gen_risks.mitigation: Limit Component 2 co-investments to a minority role with a maximum cap of $500,000 following qualified lead institutional investors, and set exposure caps in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: consider the risks related to total exposure to the same startups (through Component 1 and Component 2)

gen_risks.description: High-growth Jordanian startups may relocate their corporate headquarters to GCC countries, diminishing local employment and economic spillover benefits in Jordan.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include strict 'Jordan Investment' definitions and thresholds in Side Letters, requiring portfolio startups to maintain core operational workforce and R&D in Jordan.
gen_risks.evidence: even though some Jordanian startups relocate their headquarters to GCC countries in later growth stages

gen_risks.description: Social norms and legislative hurdles could lead to lower participation and equity investment allocation for youth- and female-led startups.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement a dedicated Gender Action Plan, target at least 30% female-led/owned beneficiaries, and partner with IFC programs like Start Mashreq.
gen_risks.evidence: there is a risk that they may not fully benefit if specific barriers to their participation are not effectively addressed.

gen_risks.description: Underlying VC fund managers may engage in fraudulent practices, mismanagement, or regulatory non-compliance, risking public fund loss.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct rigorous Operational Due Diligence (ODD) prior to fund commitments and maintain ongoing monitoring of portfolio funds' compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: monitor risks such as fraud, mismanagement, or regulatory non-compliance.

gen_risks.description: ICT sector startups supported by project capital could suffer data privacy breaches, cybersecurity failures, or aggravate digital access disparities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Screen tech startups for data protection compliance and require technical due diligence protocols covering data privacy and cybersecurity standards.
gen_risks.evidence: social risks, including poor labor and working conditions, limited stakeholder engagement, the digital divide, data privacy and security risks

gen_risks.description: Persistent reliance on traditional banking and subdued credit growth in Jordan could reduce availability of follow-on debt financing for growing SMEs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy catalytic risk capital via quasi-equity, convertible notes, and co-investments to bridge the gap left by commercial banking constraints.
gen_risks.evidence: underscored challenges such as underdeveloped financial instruments and reliance on traditional banking system with a subdued credit growth.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is rated Substantial. External economic shocks, regional instability and related uncertainties, or a downturn in global venture capital markets could reduce investor confidence and slow private capital mobilization. Additionally, Jordan's nascent venture capital market and competition from more developed ecosystems in neighboring countries may impact startup retention and funding.

Other risks are rated Substantial and relate to geopolitical risk. Jordan's strategic location makes it susceptible to a complex set of geopolitical challenges that have intensified in recent years, due to the current Conflict in the Middle East and its repercussions for investment, trade, and tourism in the region. Increasing geopolitical risks may prompt adjustments in policy and budgetary priorities and/or contribute to delays in implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: By combining regional and global diplomacy, building international partnerships, staying the course on political and economic modernization reforms, implementing prudent fiscal policies, and strategic security measures, Jordan has maintained its resilience and stability despite continuous crises.
